name: neglected_step
summary: A creative tutorial breaking down the process of sound designing an action scene from John Wick. The editing blends dynamic talking-head commentary with timeline screen captures, movie clips, and bold visual markers synced to sound cues.

captions.notes: Does not use standard continuous dialogue captions; instead flashes large single uppercase action words on screen to highlight Foley beats.

headline.notes: Uses colored horizontal bars to organize and track workflow stages, alongside occasional big center title cards.

callouts.notes: Uses hand-drawn colored outlines and rectangular highlighter overlays on timeline clips and video footage.

transitions.notes: Fast hard cuts between host and timeline UI, enhanced with audio J/L cuts for smooth sound playback.

rules: Cut immediately to the timeline UI when demonstrating a specific sound sample
Display bold kinetic text on screen precisely when an action hit or sword slash occurs
Punch in on the speaker's face to emphasize comedic reactions and disbelief
Use a color-coded numbered layer graphic as a recurring chapter menu
Maintain high speech density by trimming dead air between phrases
Show full-screen A/B playback before and after adding a new sound design pass
Overlay the speaker via picture-in-picture during full action playback to maintain connection
Highlight specific timeline tracks with a contrasting stroke or zoom-in
Switch between full-screen timeline, talking head, and film playback every 2 to 4 seconds.
Place the editor in a rounded picture-in-picture corner box during extended film playback.
Punch in dynamically on timeline waveforms when demonstrating specific sound effects.
Use uppercase single-word impact titles tracked to screen motion for emphasized action.
avoid: Lengthy static screen recordings without cursor or audio movement
Complex 3D transition wipes or artificial lens flares
Never let a static timeline view sit without zoom punch-ins for more than 5 seconds.
Avoid fancy wipe or dissolve transitions.
